answer: Each identity must post a bond of 500 quartz locked for 30 epochs, and the registry admits one credential per hardware root. An attacker forging N identities locks 500N quartz and loses 100 percent of it if any single bond is slashed within the delta window. Splitting identities fails because the marginal cost per fake stays 500 quartz, shared slashing propagates across the cluster, and independent jurors detect clones before the horizon expires.
